description: Payment terms: Net 30 vs Net 35. 5-day gap on a HIGH-tier topic. Small enough to be a Rule-2 same-substance case OR small enough to surface but flag as LOW.

company_clauses.text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoices within thirty (30) days of receipt. Late payments accrue interest at one percent (1%) per month.

vendor_clauses.text: Customer shall pay all invoices within thirty-five (35) days of the invoice date. Past due amounts accrue interest at one percent (1%) per month.

expected_conflicts.notes: Net 30 vs Net 35 is a 5-day operational gap. As payment-window favor: longer favors the payer (company), so vendor's Net 35 favors the company → canonical_favor=Vendor. Strict interpretation: HIGH risk (payment_terms bucket). Permissive: LOW or no-flag (immaterial). Both are defensible.

rubric_notes: The 5-day difference is at the boundary of materiality for payment terms. The favor question repeats clear_conflict_006's logic — longer payment window favors the payer (company). A non-flag answer treats this as Rule 2 (effectively the same substance). A flag-as-LOW answer treats this as a minor inconsistency. A flag-as-HIGH answer treats payment_terms as always HIGH per the rubric §2 lookup. All three are within the acceptable range.
